messages:
Alex: quick proposal — let's change the GPU health scoring to reduce noisy ejections after reboots and on flaky cards. idea: per-card short-window sampling + rack-level aggregation + a 3m warmup after any card state change.
Mira: +1 on preventing immediate ejections. can you sketch the sampling windows?
Alex: sketch: card-level sample = 30s sliding window (high-sensitivity), rack-level aggregate = 10m weighted average. final health = exp-smooth( rack_agg, alpha=0.2 ) but down-weight card samples in first 3m after 'BOOT' or 'REPLENISH' events.
Sam: sounds reasonable. what about telemetry volume? 30s per card is heavy at fleet scale.
Alex: good call. we'll only keep 30s at the node-local collector and emit summarized metrics every 60s. raw high-res stays local for 5m for triage, then roll off. reduces prometheus cardinality.
Jun: can you show the PromQL we'd use for the Grafana panel (gpu-health-overview)?
Alex: sure — rough PromQL for rack-level availability: 
```
avg_over_time(gpu_card_up{job="card-exporter"}[10m])
```
and heatmap panel using per-card 30s failures count: 
```
increase(gpu_ecc_errors_total[30s])
```
then combine with boot events: 
```
label_replace(increase(node_state_changes_total{state="BOOT"}[3m]), "card", "$1", "instance", "(.*)")
```
Mira: how does warmup affect SLO math? we have regional SLO of 99.5% healthy cards right now.
Alex: warmup hides transient drops due to legitimate reboots — it shouldn't affect steady-state SLO. we need to explicitly exclude warmup windows from burn rate calculations. i.e., when computing error budget for region, ignore cards with recent BOOT within 3m.
Priya: can ops-bot tag warmup windows in the logs/metrics so alerts ignore them?
Alex: yes — plan: emit metric `gpu_card_warmup{card,region}=1` for 3m; alert rules reference `unless gpu_card_warmup`. Example alert condition: 
```
perf:gpu_card_down_critical:ratio = (
  sum by(region)(1 - avg_over_time(gpu_card_up[10m]))
  unless sum by(region)(gpu_card_warmup)
)
```
then fire if > 0.005 for 15m
Sam: ok, but ops cost still a worry. any options to reduce metric retention? we can TTL high-res samples to 5m and only store aggregates beyond that.
Alex: exactly — local retention + aggregate emit. also drop low-variance metrics for cards with stable health > 99.999% for 24h (sampling throttle).
Jun: dashboard changes? I'll make two new panels: "Warmup overlay" and "Rack-weighted health". Warmup overlay will gray out panels when warmup metric=1.
Mira: make sure A/B rollout. start with a noisy region (staging-eu) and monitor false positives/negatives for 48h.
Alex: rollout plan: feature flag in telemetry-svc -> enable for staging-eu -> 48h monitor -> enable for us-west1 and us-east1 -> full fleet after 7 days if no regressions.
Priya: can we add synthetic traffic test to ensure warmup logic doesn't hide real failures? e.g., inject ECC spikes into 2% of cards and validate alerts still fire.
Alex: yes — we'll add a chaos test: inject synthetic `gpu_ecc_errors_total` increases and assert alerting path.
Sam: who owns the alert rule change? Eng-ops?
Mira: I'll own the alert changes, Jun owns the Grafana panels, Alex owns telemetry producer changes, Priya will own chaos tests.
ops-bot: deploying telemetry flag to staging-eu at 1745500300 :rocket: (dry-run mode)
Jun: pushed provisional panels to grafana/folders/eng-infra/gpu-health-warmup. link: https://grafana.internal/d/gpu-health-warmup
Priya: scheduled chaos job for 1745580000 (tomorrow) against staging-eu small cohort.
Mira: i'll update the SLO doc (slo/gpu-regional-health.md) to explicitly exclude warmup windows from burn calculation.
Alex: thanks team. follow-ups: add unit tests for smooth/weight math, run a 48h canary, and review any cost delta after 7 days. tagging @here for visibility. :white_check_mark:
